source_text: I have briefed codex-19 that they should continue to work on a validated Lean port.  They will use your transpiled code as a guide, but from now on they will not be stopped by any bugs in that code.  They will notify you if they find Transpiler bugs and then they will work around those bugs with fresh Lisp code.  Your responsibility remains the transpiler itself.  You cannot simply wait for codex-19 to surface bugs to fix one at a time.  You should instead focus on extending the transpiler so that it can cover all of the Python to date, as well as address any bugs that are brought to your attention.

㊥ (responsibility) I own proactive transpiler development and reported transpilation defects. Codex-19 owns the validated Lean port.

㊢ (completed) Commit `a722551` adds ordinary class decorators. Auditing all **690 tracked Python modules** at `11a8074` showed translation coverage advancing **684 → 685**, with five remaining rejections.

㊬ (validation) CPython-versus-SBCL tests pass for decorator ordering, replacement and failure behavior, plus adjacent function-decorator, generic-class and dataclass regressions. These ran against a clean committed runtime.

㊭ (next work) The remaining translation gaps are two `__new__` implementations and three async/generator cases. Runtime linking and initialization require separate validation; translation counts do not establish execution success. [Coverage and remaining failures](/home/joe/code/mfuton-sbcl/lisp/transpiler/evidence/full-source-20261004/summary.json).
